content.text:
I found one layout bug on the About page and fixed it. It isn't clearly the cause of what you noticed, though. The repo has a single commit, so I couldn't tell which change broke it and went by screenshots instead.

At desktop width and on narrow phones the page looked fine. In between, at tablet widths just above the 720px breakpoint (768px, for example), the "How it started" text was squeezed into a 192px column. The cause was `.story` in `site/css/pages.css`, which used `grid-template-columns: 1fr 480px`, so the image kept a fixed 480px and the text got whatever was left.

I changed it to two equal flexible columns. The image now scales with its column up to 480px (`width: 100%; max-width: 480px`). In the stacked layout below 720px it aligns left.

Column widths after the change:

| Viewport | Text column | Image column |
|---|---|---|
| 768px | 336px | 336px |
| 900px | 402px | 402px |
| 1280px | 472px | 472px |

There is no horizontal overflow at 375, 600, 768, 900 or 1280px, and the 16 functional tests pass.

If you were seeing something different, tell me what you see (which viewport, and which part of the page). I didn't find anything else wrong in the About page's HTML or CSS.

STATUS: DONE
